schema.description: Raw bytes of the gzipped tar archive.

200.description: Gzipped tar archive of the on-appliance log bundle.

Content-Disposition.description:
Attachment filename of the form
`broker_log_<device_id>_<timestamp>.tar.gz`, where
`device_id` is the broker's `PLATFORM_ID` (or
`unknown` if not yet registered) and `timestamp` is
rendered as `%b_%d_%Y_%H_%M_%S` (e.g.
`May_17_2026_10_30_00`).

Synchronous startup failure (e.g., Redis read error from
`build_bundle_filename`, or pre-stream audit log emission
failure). Streaming failures are NOT mapped to 500 — see
the operation description.

summary: Configure (or disable) a physical network interface

body.description:
When `interface_type='static'`, both `address` and `netmask`
must additionally be non-empty (enforced by Pydantic's
`_static_requires_address` model validator).

gateway.description: Default gateway. Optional; at most one gateway is allowed across all interfaces.

interface_type.description:
`''` disables the interface. `'dhcp'` enables DHCP. `'static'`
requires `address` and `netmask`.

is_admin.description: Whether this interface serves the broker's admin UI.

body.description: Body for `setInternalSubnet`. The `docker_subnet` is the parent address pool, not a single bridge subnet — see the endpoint description for pool semantics.

docker_subnet.description:
Parent address pool CIDR. Per-network bridges are carved
from this pool at `parent_prefix + 2` width (e.g., a `/18`
yields `/20` bridges).

body.description:
`pwd` follows tristate semantics — omit (`null`) to preserve
the stored password, set to `""` to clear it, set to a value
to replace it. When `proxy_type` is non-empty, both `host` and
`port` are required (cross-field rule, enforced server-side).
Body for `setNtp`. Replaces the broker's NTP server list (between 1 and 10 entries).

items.description: Hostname or IP of an NTP server.

summary: Install a custom SSL serving certificate

body.description: Body for `setSslCertificate`. The `ssl_key` and `ssl_cert` are base64-encoded PEM payloads, each capped at ~1.4 MiB encoded.

ssl_cert.description: Base64-encoded PEM certificate chain (capped at ~1.4 MiB encoded).

ssl_key.description: Base64-encoded PEM private key (capped at ~1.4 MiB encoded).

ssl_key_name.description: Optional display name for the certificate (max 128 chars).

summary: Install a custom trusted CA bundle

body.description: Body for `setTrustedCa`. The `file` is a base64-encoded PEM CA bundle, capped at ~1.4 MiB encoded.

file.description: Base64-encoded PEM CA bundle (capped at ~1.4 MiB encoded).

token.description:
Registration token previously issued by the tenant-side
`POST /public_api/v1/brokers/registration_token/`.

400.description:
Pydantic validation failure (missing or empty `token`), or

tenant call was made.

parameters.description: The opaque action identifier returned by a prior mutating call.

(This read-only poll endpoint performs no cluster-member

summary: Get an applet's configuration and status

200.description:
Applet configuration + status. The schema variant is
selected by the `applet` discriminator field, which always
equals the path's `applet_name`.

Edit accepted. The configuration is applied **asynchronously** —
the body is an acknowledgement `{ "status": "activating" }`, not
the applied config. Poll [`getApplet`](#operation/getApplet) (or
[`getBrokers`](#operation/getBrokers)) to observe the config once
it has been applied.

summary: Activate an applet with a configuration

body.description:
Optional body for [`deactivateApplet`](#operation/deactivateApplet).
The body itself is optional; when absent or `save_config` is
omitted, the broker preserves the applet's prior configuration so
a later `activate` without a body restores it.

save_config.description:
`true` (default) — preserve the applet's current configuration
for later reactivation. `false` — drop the configuration; a
subsequent `activate` requires a full body.

summary: Download the WEC/WEF client certificate as a PFX archive

body.description: Body for `downloadWefCert`. The `password` (min 5 chars) is the PFX export password.

password.description:
Export password applied to the PFX archive returned to the
caller. The password protects the embedded private key on the
wire; the customer-facing minimum length is 5 characters.

schema.description: Raw bytes of the PFX archive.

200.description: PFX archive containing the WEF client certificate.

body.description:
Optional filters for [`getBrokers`](#operation/getBrokers). Omit
the body entirely to return every broker.

name.description:
Filter on `device_name`. A value containing shell-style
wildcards (`*`, `?`) is matched with `fnmatch`
(case-insensitive); a value without wildcards is matched
exactly (case-sensitive). Multiple values are OR-combined.

200.description:
Brokers matching the request. An unfiltered request returns a
JSON array (possibly empty). A filtered request that matches
nothing returns JSON `null` — hence the schema is nullable.

body.description:
Patch for a single broker. Any field omitted from the body is left
unchanged. Server-side validation rules are described per-field
below.

allow_monitoring.description: Whether the broker reports monitoring metrics.

auto_upgrade.description:
Master switch for auto-upgrade. When `true`, `upgrade_window`
should also be provided.

broker_ui_password.description:
New broker web-UI admin password (write-only; never returned
by `getBrokers`).

internal_network.description: Internal network CIDR. Must parse as an IPv4 network.

name.description: New display name for the broker.

ntp.description: List of NTP server hostnames or IPs.

ssh_enabled.description: Whether SSH access to the broker is enabled.

ssh_keys.description:
Authorized SSH public keys. Each entry must start with one of
`ssh-rsa`, `ssh-ed25519`, `ssh-dss`, `ecdsa-sha2-`.

ssl_crt_file_name.description: Display name for the SSL certificate file.

ssl_key_file_name.description: Display name for the SSL key file.

webui_port.description:
Port the broker's web UI listens on. Must parse as an integer
in `[1, 65535]`.

customer_uami_serverless_id.description: The resource ID of your existing Azure User-Assigned Managed Identity to use for serverless function scanning. uami_mode.description:
Controls whether Cortex creates and manages the User-Assigned Managed Identities (UAMIs) used by the outpost for each security capability, or whether you provide your own. Only applicable when `cloud_provider` is `AZURE`.

- `cortex_managed`: (Default) Cortex automatically creates and manages the UAMIs required for each enabled security capability.
- `customer_managed`: You provide existing UAMIs for each capability. Use this when your organization requires control over managed identity assignments. When set to `customer_managed`, provide the relevant `customer_uami_*` fields for each capability you want to enable.

200.description: Ok. Returns a paginated list of unified rule pairs. Each item contains the linked AppSec and Cloud Security (CSPM) rule details.

body.description:
The request body for creating a unified rule pair. Both the `cspm` and `appsec` rule definitions are required.

The endpoint creates the CSPM rule first, then creates the AppSec rule with the CSPM rule ID automatically injected to link the two rules. If the AppSec rule creation fails, the CSPM rule is automatically rolled back.

appsec.description: The definition for the AppSec IaC rule to create. This rule evaluates IaC configurations in code repositories. The CSPM rule ID is automatically injected to link the two rules.

cspm.description: The definition for the CSPM rule to create. This rule evaluates deployed cloud infrastructure at runtime.

201.description: Created. The unified rule pair was created successfully. The top-level `id` field is the AppSec rule ID and serves as the primary identifier for all subsequent operations on this unified rule.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the unified rule to retrieve. This is the **AppSec rule ID**, which serves as the primary identifier for the unified rule pair. You can retrieve this value from the `id` field in the response of [List unified rules](#operation/ListUnifiedRules).
parameters.name: ruleId

200.description: Ok. Returns the full details of the unified rule pair, including both the AppSec and CSPM rule objects.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the unified rule to update. This is the **AppSec rule ID**, which serves as the primary identifier for the unified rule pair. You can retrieve this value from the `id` field in the response of [List unified rules](#operation/ListUnifiedRules).
parameters.name: ruleId

body.description: The request body for updating a unified rule pair. Include only the rule object or fields you want to update. You can update the CSPM rule, the AppSec rule, or both in a single request.

appsec.description: The fields to update on the AppSec rule. Include only the fields you want to change.

cspm.description: The fields to update on the CSPM rule. Include only the fields you want to change.

200.description: Ok. Both rules were updated successfully. Returns the updated unified rule pair.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the unified rule to delete. This is the **AppSec rule ID**, which serves as the primary identifier for the unified rule pair. You can retrieve this value from the `id` field in the response of [List unified rules](#operation/ListUnifiedRules).
parameters.name: ruleId

204.description: Deleted. Both the AppSec and CSPM rules were deleted successfully. No content is returned.

207.description: Multi-Status. The AppSec rule is always deleted first. This status is returned when the AppSec rule was deleted successfully but the subsequent Cloud Security rule deletion failed, potentially leaving the Cloud Security rule orphaned. The response body contains per-rule status details (success for appsec, failed for cspm).

field.description:
The field to use for filtering results.

For the complete list of supported fields, operators, and values, see [Vulnerability Intelligence Filter Fields](https://app.gitbook.com/s/FK89utN7l3ilSek2DmU5/vulnerability-intelligence/vulnerability-intelligence-papi-tables#vulnerability-intelligence-filter-fields).

operator.description:
Comparison operator to use with the filter. Allowed values depend on the filters field.
- **contains**/**not_contains**: use with affected_cpu_archs, affected_versions, cvss_severity, distro, package_name, release, vulnerability_id
- **eq**/**neq**: use with distro, cvss_severity, cvss_score, package_name, release, vulnerability_id
- **gte**/**lte**: use with cvss_score, last_modified
- **range**: use with last_modified
- **relative_timestamp**: use with last_modified

value.description:
Values for filtering the results.
- *array[string]*: use with affected_cpu_archs, affected_versions
- *string*: use with cvss_score, distro, release, package_name, vulnerability_id
- *integer*: use with last_modified
- *number*: use with cvss_score

field.description: Identifies the field the filter is matching.

operator.description:
Identifies the comparison operator you want to use for this filter. Allowed values depend on the filter used.
- **contains**/**not_contains**: use with attack_vector, cvss_score_source, cvss_severity_source, cvss_version , distribution_and_releases, package_names, reported_exploited_by, vendors, vulnerability_id
- **eq**/**neq**: use with attack_vector, cisa_kev, cvss_score, cvss_score_source, cvss_severity_source, cvss_version, epss_score, vulnerability_id
- **gte**/**lte**: use with cvss_score, epss score, first_published, last_modified
- **range**: use with first_published, last_modified
- **relative_timestamp**: use with first_published, last_modified

value.description:
Values for filtering the results.
- *array[string]*: use with affected_cpu_archs, distribution_and_releases, package_names, reported_exploited_by
- *boolean*: cisa_kev
- *string*: use with attack_vector, cvss_score, cvss_severity, cvss_score_source, cvss_severity_source, cvss_version, vulnerability_id
- *integer*: use with first_published, last_modified
- *number*: use with cvss_score, epss_score
